prompt: A tall, narrow gothic bell tower of a Victorian harbor cathedral, seen from street level far away, standing alone and filling the frame from its broad stone base at the bottom edge to the tip of its spire near the top. The tower is built of soot-blackened, rain-soaked granite blocks with tall pointed arch windows that are pitch black inside, an open belfry near the top where a large dark iron bell hangs silent, and a crooked slate spire that leans to one side, snapped near its tip, with a bent iron weathervane hanging loose. Deep cracks run down the stonework, broken slates are missing from the spire, and dark streaks of grime run from every ledge. Painted in a dark Victorian oil painting style with soft blended shading in near-black blue and charcoal tones, heavy shadow over most of the tower, lit dimly and evenly with no bright highlights. Plain flat solid bright green background, nothing else behind the subject.
